x: Welcome to Radii Office Radii Office is a TU.dusk(free), TU.dusk(open-source) suite of apps that runs in your browser, works offline and also comes as desktop apps. There is nothing to sign up for to write, draw, plan or calculate, and your files stay on your computer unless you choose to share them! New here? Open Writeout, type Hello and press Enter. You just used Keydown, the formatting language every app shares. The Keydown guide explains the rest! {aqua}

L.packet(Getting started) covers things every app shares: looks, files, sharing, offline use and privacy! G.packet(Apps) has one guide per app, written from the real buttons and tabs! TU.packet(Keydown) is the full formatting language, including a reference of every tag, style and block! T.packet(Languages) covers BitLang, Plume and the Suave programming language! C.packet(Reference) has the FAQ and troubleshooting! Press Ctrl+K {key} (or / {key}) anywhere on this page to search all of it! {wavy Three ideas to remember blue}

1. T Everything is Keydown. Documents, notes, slides, messages and wiki articles are all Keydown text, so a tag you learn in one app works in all of them! 2. C Files are yours. Apps save plain files you can open in other Radii apps, and every app can export what you made! 3. B Looks are a switch. Every app has the same three layouts, so you can pick the one you like best, and your documents never change! - This site is itself written in Keydown and drawn with Dark Keydown, the version that fades to white instead of transparent so every style looks right on a dark page!
Layouts and themes Every Radii Office app can wear three different looks. They change how the app is arranged, not what it does, and your documents are identical in all of them. {aqua}

B Nova is the default. It is flat and soft, with Vadivam icons, rounded corners and a File screen in the same style! G New is a ribbon like Microsoft Office, with tabs along the top and groups of commands under them! PR Classic is the original look: a glass sidebar with gel buttons, and the page in a bright frame!

1. Open the T.packet(View) tab (or the T.packet(Help) tab in apps without one) and look for T.packet(Layout), or press T.packet(Layout) in the ribbon! 2. Pick one of the cards. The app switches right away, and the choice is remembered on this computer! Some apps have a T.packet(Themes) or T.packet(Look) button in the sidebar that opens the same cards! Your files do not change Switching layouts only moves buttons around. Open a document in Classic, switch to Nova, and it is exactly the same file!

The File button (top left in New and Nova, in the sidebar in Classic) opens a full-page screen with the commands that are about the whole file: New, Open, Save a Copy, Export, Print and Info. Which commands appear depends on the app. Cabinet, for example, has Drawers, and Mainkey has Open and Export!
Writeout and Bitbook also have a fourth layout, G.packet(Poolside), a glassy look in cyan, blue and orange. It exists only in those two apps!
Apps follow their layout's colors. This documentation page has its own switch: the moon button at the top right changes between dark and light, and remembers your choice!
Files, saving and versions Radii Office apps save ordinary files that you own. This page explains the file types, where your work is kept, and how to get it out. {aqua}

Extension Made by What it is --- --- --- G.bubble(.kd) Writeout, OpenDB A Keydown document: a short header and then readable text TU.bubble(.kn) Bitbook A Keydown note T.bubble(.ka) Amber A presentation C.bubble(.kv) Inkpath A vector drawing B.bubble(.kb) Mainkey A record database PR.bubble(.kfe) PR.bubble(.kfv) PR.bubble(.kfa) Formly An editable form, a viewable form, and the answers PK.bubble(.ics) PK.bubble(.kh) Hexa Calendar events (standard iCalendar) and Hexa's own format R.bubble(.tk) Taskra A to-do list O.bubble(.kc) Cabinet A drawer shared as a file Because the Keydown files are plain text, you can open them in any text editor, and Writeout and Bitbook can open each other's files!

C.gem(In the browser.) Apps keep your documents on this computer, in the browser's own storage, so they are there when you come back. Nothing is uploaded! B.gem(In a file on your computer.) Use Share Keep a file on this computer (Chrome, Edge and Opera) to link a document to a real file. The app then saves to it automatically! PR.gem(On a shared link.) Sharing is separate and always your choice. See Sharing and live editing! Clearing site data deletes browser copies If you clear your browser's site data, documents kept only in the browser are removed. Export or keep a file on your computer for anything important!

Writeout, Bitbook and other apps share a documents library. Each document has its own address ending in ?file and an id, so the address always reopens that document. Opening an app without an address reopens the document you used last!

Choose File Version history (or Review Version History in Writeout) to see earlier copies of a document. Apps take a snapshot as you work, and TU Save Version takes one on purpose. Pick one to preview it and restore it!

G.pixel(Save a Copy) and PK Export (on the File screen) write a file to your computer! Writeout exports PDF, Word ( .docx ), OpenDocument ( .odt ), plain text and EPUB, and both Writeout and Bitbook can PK Print ! Inkpath exports SVG and PNG, and Imbuer and Mainkey import and export CSV! Hexa exports .ics , and Zonerider exports glTF, OBJ and STL! Every app's data is yours: there is no lock-in, and the source is public!
Sharing and live editing There are two ways to work with other people: send a C file , or work together on a C live link . {aqua}
Every app can save its work as a file (see Files). Email it, put it in a drawer in Cabinet, or drop it anywhere. The other person opens it in the same app!

Apps with a TU Share tab (Cabinet, Mainkey, Formly, Hexa, Taskra, Delta and others) have a Share & Chat button. It starts a live session. Everyone who opens the link sees changes as they happen, and a chat panel lets you talk while you work. No account is needed!

Overshare is a hosted place to share documents. Sign up, link a Writeout, Taskra or other Radii document, and everyone with the link edits it live. It also has PK Groups , like a team site, and keeps a history of changes. Overshare has three themes, New, Nova and Classic!

R.belt(Phosphor) is a server-based chat app with servers, channels, roles, direct messages, voice and custom emojis! O.belt(Antimony) is a message board with spaces, posts and replies! GL.belt(Beta) is a microblog, and L Mintcode hosts code. See Community apps!

You share They can --- --- A file Open and edit their own copy A Share & Chat link See and edit live while the session is open An Overshare edit link Edit live (you can limit this in Link Settings) An Overshare view link Read only Keep editing links private Anyone who has an edit link can change the document. Treat it like a password, and use a view link when people only need to read!
Offline and desktop apps {aqua}

Radii Office saves itself for offline use the first time you visit. After that, the apps open without a connection, and your documents are already on your computer. When you are back online, nothing needs to be synced because nothing left your computer! Things that need the internet by nature, like Phosphor chat, Beta, Mintcode, Overshare and getting real email in Yuzu, only work online. Everything that edits your own files works offline!

GL.bottle(As an app from the browser.) In Chrome or Edge, use the install button in the address bar to add an app to your dock or desktop! Y.bottle(Desktop apps.) Open Products and press GL.bucket(Download) on any app for a Mac, Windows or Linux build. Desktop apps open and save files directly on your computer, and they are rebuilt whenever the site changes! L.bottle(Phones.) Most apps have a GL.bucket(Mobile) button that opens a layout designed for small screens!

Downloads are signed so you can check that nobody changed them. The public keys and fingerprints are in /signing/ on this site, and the pages have integrity hashes on their scripts. The details are in Privacy and security!
In any app, use File Open to pick a file from your computer. Desktop apps can open and save files directly on disk!
Privacy and security {aqua}
Documents, notes, sheets and drawings are kept in your browser or in files you choose. The apps do not upload them, and there are no accounts to make for ordinary use!

h: What goes online, and only when you ask
x: Share & Chat, Overshare, Phosphor, Antimony, Beta, Mintcode and Yuzu mail send what you put in them to their own servers, because that is how they work! C.torpedo(Pictures from OpenDB) are fetched from this site when you insert them! B.torpedo(Math) is drawn by KaTeX, which is bundled with the site!

PK.bottle(Security headers) on every page: no other site can frame Radii Office, and scripts and styles come from known places! R.bottle(Signed downloads) with published keys and fingerprints in /signing/ ! O.bottle(Integrity hashes) on loaded scripts, so a changed file is refused! GL.bottle(Safe Keydown.) Text drawn by Keydown in shared places (messages, posts, mail) is cleaned again after it is drawn, so scripts and frames in it are removed! Y.bottle(Mail content.) Real email in Yuzu is shown inside a sandboxed frame with a strict policy, and pictures from the internet are blocked until you press O.packet(Load pictures)!
If you find a security problem, please tell the team using the contact link on the home page before posting it publicly. The code of conduct is here!
The suite is free software. OpenDB content is CC0 (public domain), and fonts and icons keep their own free licenses, listed in ATTRIBUTIONS.md and ATTRIBUTIONS-FONTS.md in the source!

Writeout C Documents Writeout is the word processor of the suite. It has real pages, a Navigation pane, a status bar and a ribbon that works like Microsoft Word, and everything you write is Keydown text! Open Writeout · Phone version {wavy Writeout blue}

Tab What you will find --- --- PK.bucket(Home) Clipboard, Font, Paragraph, Styles (including Keydown Styles), Editing and Margin Marks R.bucket(Insert) New Page, Table, Picture, Link, Header & Footer, Symbols, Captions, Cards & Blocks, Badges, Templates, Equation, and Bulleted and Numbered Lists O.bucket(Layout) Margins, Orientation, Size, Pages View, Print Preview, Color Preview, Page Number Format, Watermark, Page Border and Line Spacing GL.bucket(References) Table of Contents, Footnotes, Cross-references, Citations, Sources, Bibliography and Mail Merge Y.bucket(Review) Word Count, Find & Replace, Comments, Track Changes, Read Aloud, Un-format and Re-format, the Annotator, Ink Drawing, Readability, Word Goal, Version History and Protect Document L.bucket(View) View, Visual and Source modes, Pages, Continuous and Focus views, Zoom, and the Layout switch G.bucket(Help) Help Deck, Keydown Guide and Shortcuts

The GL.flag(View) tab has three modes, and you can switch any time without losing anything: GL.marker(View) shows the finished page. Click to edit, and Keydown tags turn into formatting as you type them! Y.marker(Visual) is the same page with the formatting controls visible, like a classic word processor! L.marker(Source) shows the raw Keydown text, with colors for tags, headings, chips and code. Press GL.flag(Tab) to insert an indent (a leading )!

Type a tag and press T.flag(Space), and it becomes formatting. Press T.flag(Enter) at the end of a line to format every tag still on that line. For example: A heading This is bold , this is italic , and this is code . ++R+A glossy red chip++ Remember this Use T.flag(Un-format) to turn a whole page back into tags, and T.flag(Re-format) to format everything again. Tags that could not be formatted are underlined so mistakes are easy to find. The full language is in the Keydown guide!

C.dusk(New Page) (Insert tab, or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter) adds a real page break, written as ::pagebreak . The R.flag(Pages) list in the side pane shows every page! B.dusk(Print Preview) shows the true page size and margins, and R.flag(Color Preview) shows grayscale or color-blind views! PR.dusk(Margins, Orientation and Size) are in Layout, and are saved in the file's header!

Documents are saved as .kd files. File Home lists every saved document so you can rename or switch between them, and Share Keep a file on this computer keeps a real file updated as you type (Chrome, Edge and Opera). Export gives PDF, Word, OpenDocument, plain text and EPUB. See Files for the rest!

Review Comments and PR.flag(Track Changes) work like other word processors! GL.gem(Version History) (and PR.flag(Save Version)) lets you look at and restore earlier copies! Share & Chat edits the same document live with other people. See Sharing!

Cards & Blocks adds document blocks like a table of contents, a cover page, callouts, columns, tabs, checklists and footnotes lists. See Document blocks! G.spotlight(Badge) opens a picker for small labeled chips! TU.spotlight(Equation) inserts math in LaTeX, drawn by KaTeX! T.spotlight(Templates) starts from a ready-made layout! C.spotlight(3D scenes) and Inkpath drawings can be embedded, and fonts like Kubasta and Monogram are bundled!

Bitbook PR Notes Bitbook is a notebook with real pages. It uses the same Keydown engine as Writeout, plus a set of small skills (gadgets) and a programming language called BitLang for little programs inside your notes! Open Bitbook · Phone version {wavy Bitbook green}

Tab What you will find --- --- G.spotlight(Home) Clipboard, Basic Text, Paragraph, Styles, Keydown Styles and Find TU.spotlight(Insert) New Page, New Note, Table, File Attachment, Pictures, OpenDB Images, Inkpath drawings, 3D Scene, Image on Top, Link, Equation, Time Stamp, Symbol, To Do Tag and Bullets T.spotlight(Skills) Chips (Uni-Chip, Custom Chip, Unique Styles, Custom CSS) and Gadgets (Jumper, BeepBox Song, Pixel Sprite, Custom Emoji, Time Capsule, Flashcard, Focus Timer, Dice Roller, Programs, Highlight, Annotate) C.spotlight(View) View, Visual and Source modes, Pages View, Print Preview, Page Color, Rule Lines, Zoom and Layout B.spotlight(Help) Help Deck and the BitLang Guide
Notes are saved as .kn files. Like Writeout, a note can have several real pages ( ::pagebreak ), a Pages view and a Print Preview. Writeout and Bitbook open each other's files!

Skills turn a tag into a small working thing inside your text: The O.aurora(Skills) tab lists them under Gadgets : Jumper, BeepBox Song, Pixel Sprite, Custom Emoji, Time Capsule, Flashcard, Focus Timer, Dice Roller, Programs, Highlight and Annotate. Click one to insert it at the caret, and its tag appears in the text so you can edit it later in Source mode. O.aurora(Chips) has the Uni-Chip, Custom Chip, Unique Styles and Custom CSS tools! O.aurora(Annotate) and O.aurora(Highlight) mark up text with pens, which are written as Keydown tags. See Annotator pens!

A BitLang program lives in a note. It can show text, make buttons, change how things look and react when you hover. The BitLang guide has the language! Programs and editing If you want a program to keep running while you read, stay in TU.aurora(View) mode and do not type in the page while it runs. Typing rebuilds the page, which stops running programs!

Amber GL Slides Amber is a slide studio with glossy 3D shapes, spring-animated menus and a full-screen presentation mode. Its ribbon works like PowerPoint, and slides are Keydown text. Presentations are saved as .ka files! Open Amber · Phone version {wavy Amber orange}

Tab What you will find --- --- TU.flag(Home) New Slide, Font, Paragraph, Spacing, Shapes, Arrange and Rotate & Flip T.flag(Insert) Table, Chart, Icons, Diagram, Footer & Numbers, OpenDB Images, Shapes, Aero Chip, Text Box and Annotate (Draw) C.flag(Keydown) Re-format Slide, Un-format Slide, Keydown Text Box and Keydown Styles B.flag(Design) Themes, Format Background and Apply to All Slides PR.flag(Transitions) Preview, Effect Options and Timing PK.flag(Animations) Preview, Add Animation, Animation Pane and Timing R.flag(Slide Show) From Beginning, From Current Slide, Presenter View and Hide Slide O.flag(View) Normal, Slide Sorter and Notes views, Zoom and Layout

1. Press B.marker(New Slide) and pick a layout! 2. Type into a text box. Keydown tags work there: use Insert Aero Chip or the Keydown tab for chips and styles! 3. Add shapes, tables, charts and diagrams from the Insert tab! 4. Pick a theme in B.marker(Design), and add transitions and animations! 5. Press B.marker(From Beginning) to present full screen. B.marker(Presenter View) is under Slide Show!

Shapes can be rotated, flipped and given opacity and shadows (Home Rotate & Flip)! The GL.marker(Slide Sorter) view shows every slide at once! Annotate (Draw) on the Insert tab lets you draw on a slide!

Imbuer G Spreadsheet Imbuer is a spreadsheet with an Excel-style ribbon, formulas, charts and number formats. Its cells understand Keydown text styles, and sheets import and export as CSV! Open Imbuer · Phone version {wavy Imbuer teal}

B.aurora(A grid) with selection, editing, copy and paste, find and replace, and sheet tabs along the bottom! PR.aurora(Formulas) with autocomplete, so typing SU suggests the functions that start that way! PK.aurora(Charts) built from a selected range! R.aurora(Conditional formatting, sorting and filtering, and templates)! O.aurora(Cell formatting) for numbers, colors, borders and fonts, with Keydown in cells for chips and highlights! GL.aurora(CSV) import and export from the File screen!

Start a cell with . References like A1 and ranges like A1:B10 work as usual, and functions take arguments in parentheses. A formula bar shows what is in the selected cell! SUM(A1:A10) AVERAGE(B2:B20) IF(C2 100, "high", "low")

Inkpath PK Vector Inkpath is a vector graphics editor with box selection, live Bézier point dragging, and panning and zooming around the canvas. Drawings are saved as .kv files and export as SVG or PNG! Open Inkpath · Phone version {wavy Inkpath red}

R.bubble(Selection) with a drag box for several shapes at once! O.bubble(Path tools) with real-time Bézier node dragging, and a PR.bucket(knife) for cutting! GL.bubble(Gradient tool) (press PR.bucket(G)) with fill-line handles. Hold Shift to snap! Y.bubble(Rulers, guides and snapping), plus PR.bucket(align), PR.bucket(layers) and PR.bucket(artboards)!
Y.bucket(Blur Behind) turns a shape into frosted glass by blurring everything behind it. The effect survives export!

The C.bucket(Animate) panel adds keyframes: 1. Set a keyframe! 2. Move a shape! 3. Move the playhead and set another keyframe! You can also use presets like Fade in, Spin or Bounce. Export an SVG that plays by itself in any browser!
Choose File Export for SVG or PNG. Extra SVG features such as caps, dashes, markers, patterns, blend modes, groups and images are supported!

Peeker O PDF Peeker is a PDF editor that runs entirely in your browser, so your files are never uploaded. It uses the open-source pdf.js and pdf-lib libraries! Open Peeker · Phone version {wavy Peeker purple}

T.halo(Mark up): add text, highlights, drawings, boxes, whiteout, pictures and signatures! C.halo(Pages): rotate, reorder, duplicate and delete pages, and merge PDFs! B.halo(Forms): fill in form fields! PR.halo(Search) the text of a PDF! Edit (E) : the Edit tool turns the text and pictures already in a PDF into marks you can move, change or replace!
Peeker reads and edits the PDF inside your browser. Nothing is sent to a server, so it is safe for private paperwork!

Omicron O Web Builder Omicron is a visual builder for laying out web pages, making templates and producing HTML. Its ribbon works like Microsoft Sway, with cards, styles, tags and skills! Open Omicron · Phone version {wavy Omicron pink}

GL.packet(Position elements) visually, and use templates to start quickly! Y.packet(Export) a page as a website ZIP, or as a single HTML file with every style built in! L.packet(Insert Bitbook notes) into a page!
Omicron includes the same BitLang engine as Bitbook, so small programs can run inside pages you build. See BitLang!

Data and planning apps Five small apps handle records, forms, dates, tasks and files. They all have a G.bottle(Share) tab with Share & Chat , and they all use the same three layouts! {wavy Data and planning apps cyan}

PR Database Open Mainkey Build your own fields, then keep records in them. Search, filter and sort in a PR.bottle(Table), or browse a PR.bottle(Gallery) with live statistics! R.flag(Home) has New Record, Add Field, the Table and Gallery views, and Sort By! O.flag(Data) imports and exports .kb files and exports .csv , and has Demo Data and Clear All! GL.flag(Share) has a PR.bottle(Website Kit) and PR.bottle(Host), which can serve the database straight from your browser tab so others can open it!

PR Forms Open Formly Build a form with Y.bottle(New Form) and Y.bottle(Add Field), flip between Y.bottle(Builder) and Y.bottle(Preview), and share it as a file: .kfe is an Y.bottle(editable) form, so the other person can change it! .kfv is a Y.bottle(viewable) form that people fill in! .kfa holds the Y.bottle(answers)! Question text accepts Keydown, so chips and highlights work in forms. Share & Chat lets a group edit a form together!

G Calendar Open Hexa TU.bubble(Calendar) shows months and an agenda for events. C.bottle(Today) and C.bottle(Year) jump around! T.bubble(Boards) are columns of cards: C.bottle(New Board), C.bottle(New Column) and C.bottle(New Card)! C.bubble(Import and export) standard .ics files (so you can swap with other calendars) and Hexa's own .kh files!

C Todo Open Taskra Tasks have priorities and due dates. Filter with O.bottle(All Tasks), O.bottle(Active), O.bottle(Done) and O.bottle(Overdue), and use O.bottle(Clear Completed) to tidy up. Lists import and export as .tk files!

R Drive Open Cabinet Keep files in TU.bottle(drawers), like a file explorer. TU.bottle(New Drawer), TU.bottle(New Folder) and TU.bottle(Upload Files) are on the Home tab, and TU.bottle(Cards) or TU.bottle(List) views are in View. A whole drive downloads at once as a ZIP, and the Share tab can save a drawer as a .kc or .zip file!

Zonerider L 3D Zonerider is a 3D editor a little like Blender. Model with shapes and vertices, add light, animate with keyframes, render images and videos, and export glTF, OBJ and STL! Open Zonerider · Phone version {wavy Zonerider lime}

Y.pixel(Model): start from shapes and edit their vertices! L.pixel(Light and shade): add lights, and write your own shaders! G.pixel(Animate): set keyframes and play them back! TU.pixel(Render) still images and videos! T.pixel(Export) glTF, OBJ and STL, for other 3D tools or 3D printing! The O Help menu explains 3D scenes, shaders and animation!
Writeout and Bitbook can embed a Zonerider scene, so a document can hold a 3D model people can turn around. In Bitbook it is under Insert 3D Scene . Zonerider runs in a small embed mode for this!

Delta PK Math Delta is a math workspace in the ribbon style, or in its original Delta Classic look. It has a live graphing calculator, a LaTeX renderer and a calculator! Open Delta · Phone version Tab Use it for --- --- O.torpedo(Graph) Plot equations as you type. Add B.bucket(sliders) for values you want to change, use B.bucket(lists), and draw B.bucket(polygons) GL.torpedo(LaTeX) Write LaTeX and see it drawn, ready to copy into a document Y.torpedo(Calculator) Everyday and scientific calculations L.torpedo(Share) Share & Chat, for working on a graph together Math in documents Writeout, Bitbook and OpenDB draw math from $x^2$ and $$ ... $$ , using KaTeX. Delta's LaTeX tab is a good place to try an equation before pasting it!
Notes and mail {wavy Notes and mail green}

C Notes Open Waterflow A clear, glassy notebook. Notes live in R.marker(streams), R.marker(notebooks) and R.marker(tags), and are written in Poolside Keydown! GL.flag(Quick switcher): press Ctrl+K to jump to any note! Y.flag(Three modes): View, Visual and Source, like Writeout! L.flag(Outline) of the headings, and a R.marker(trash) you can restore from! G.flag(More): wiki links between notes, templates, tasks, a calendar, history, a writing goal, statistics, quick capture and a typewriter mode! TU.flag(Waterflow Legacy) keeps the original app, and the new Waterflow can bring its notes over!
B Mail Open Yuzu · Phone version An email app with an inbox, folders, search and compose. It has two looks: a new Outlook-style ribbon, and the original G.marker(Yuzu Classic)!

G.accent(A Yuzu address) ( name@radii-office.com ) that you make inside the app! TU.accent(Google or Microsoft accounts), which use the provider's own sign-in. The sign-in needs the app's client ID to be set up in the app's settings!
Messages you write are Keydown, so headings, chips and styles work. When you send to another Yuzu address, the message arrives with its Keydown and is drawn in full!

Mail from other services often has its own formatting. Yuzu shows the G.marker(formatted version) in a sandboxed frame: Scripts never run, and links open in a new tab! Pictures from the internet are G.marker(blocked) until you press G.marker(Load pictures)! G.spotlight(Plain text) is one click away on every message! Mail is kept in memory for Google and Microsoft accounts and is not stored by the app. Mail sent to a Yuzu address is stored on the Yuzu mail server until you delete it!
See Trigger for rules that react when your documents change!
Community apps These apps run on servers, so they need an internet connection. Each is its own site on a radii-office.com address! {wavy Community apps orange}

G Messaging phosphor.radii-office.com A Discord-style chat. Make an account and you can: Create TU.flag(servers) with TU.flag(channels), TU.flag(roles) and permissions! Send TU.flag(direct messages) and make TU.flag(group chats), and add TU.flag(friends)! Use TU.flag(custom emojis), reactions, pins, threads and polls! Join TU.flag(voice channels) (up to 8 people)! Add TU.flag(webhooks), and use slash commands like /me , /shrug , /poll and /nick ! Jump anywhere with the TU.flag(quick switcher) (Ctrl+K)! Messages are written in Keydown!
C Boards Open Antimony A free message board. Make spaces, post and reply, and watch new messages appear as they arrive!

L Microblog beta.radii-office.com Short posts with topics . You can follow people, like, reply, run polls, make lists, keep drafts and collections, set reminders and ask questions. L.flag(Outlets) are rooms for group talk, and there is a L.flag(Friends) feature. Each Beta instance picks its own usernames!
TU Code hosting mintcode.radii-office.com Host code with B.flag(Mint), a simple saves-and-lines version tool. It has repositories, stars, forks, issues and a web editor!
PR Sharing overshare.radii-office.com Share documents and work on them together. Read more in Sharing!
Phosphor, Beta, Mintcode and Antimony all draw Keydown in messages and posts. Their copy of Keydown is cleaned a second time after it is drawn, so scripts and frames can't get through!
Trigger O Automation Trigger is an automation panel. You write rules as text, and glowing pods react when your documents or a watched folder of .radii files change! Open Trigger {wavy Trigger teal}
!trigger-[sync]-Writeout- notify! Type rules like this into the panel and a pod appears for each one. The pods glow when the documents or files they watch change!
Trigger is for small chores that you would otherwise remember by hand, like noticing when a document changes. It runs in the app, on your computer!
OpenDB C Knowledge OpenDB is a free database of articles, media and papers that anyone can reuse. Everything in it is CC0 , which means public domain! Open OpenDB · Phone version {wavy OpenDB red}

An entry is a .kd file: a header with an id, type, title and tags, and then Keydown text. Types include T.bubble(article), T.bubble(image), T.bubble(paper) and T.bubble(lite)! --- format: keydown-text id: my-article type: article title: My article summary: One sentence about it. tags: [example] license: CC0-1.0 --- My article is about something. Link to another entry like [[keydown Keydown]]!
[[id words]] links to another entry. The Keydown guide and the Radii Office article are entries too!
A G.bubble(lite) is a small, runnable project stored as one entry (like a Gist). Each file sits in a ~~~ file: fence. You can G.bubble(fork), G.bubble(embed) and G.bubble(zip) a lite!
OpenDB draws its pages with the real Keydown engine, so every example in an article is the real thing, not a picture!
Because it is CC0, you can copy anything from OpenDB into your own project without asking. It is also where the full Keydown article lives, and the docs here read it directly!

Keydown guide PK.gem(Keydown) is the formatting language of Radii Office. You type short PK.gem(tags) around your words, and the words turn into formatting: headings, bold text, glossy chips, highlights, speech bubbles, tables, math, callouts, dividers and small interactive widgets. The same tags work in every app, so what you learn in Writeout works in Bitbook, Amber, Phosphor, OpenDB and this documentation page! Try it now Open Writeout, type Hello and press Enter, then type ++R+A red chip++ and press Space. Two tags, two kinds of formatting!

In L.gem(Writeout and Bitbook), a tag turns into its formatting when you press L.gem(Space) after it. Pressing L.gem(Enter) at the end of a line formats every tag left on that line! In OpenDB, Phosphor, Beta and other apps , tags are drawn whenever the text is shown! Most tags wrap your words with an opening and a closing tag, like R and . Typing \\ at the end of a formatted piece steps back out of it! TU Un-format turns a whole page back into tags, and L.gem(Re-format) formats it again, underlining any tag that could not be formatted!

Writeout, Bitbook, Amber, Waterflow, Imbuer, Formly, Yuzu mail, Phosphor, Antimony, Beta, Mintcode and OpenDB. There is also a standalone B.gem(Keydown.js) engine you can load in your own page, and Svelte components that draw Keydown!

Document blocks Reports, papers, letters, manuals and covers get their own blocks, and tables, code blocks and dividers are described here too. Everything below is the real reference text, drawn live by Keydown!

Reports, papers, letters, manuals and covers get their own blocks. All of them work in Writeout, Bitbook, Amber and anywhere else Keydown runs, print cleanly, and turn back into plain text when you Un-format. One line each: ::toc 3 numbered Contents builds a table of contents from your headings (the number is the deepest heading level, and numbered adds 1.2.3 numbers). Click an entry to jump. ::cover Title Subtitle Author Date is a cover page that ends with a page break. ::banner Title Subtitle blue is a colored title band. ::wordcount shows words, reading time and characters; ::date (or ::date iso , short , year ) writes today's date. ::footnotes Notes lists every footnote, ::lof lists figures and ::lot lists tables. ::stamp DRAFT red is a tilted rubber stamp, ::watermark CONFIDENTIAL puts a big faint word behind the page. ::sign Name, Title and ::signatures Alice Bob draw signature lines. ::keywords one, two, three makes keyword pills, ::lorem 3 fills in placeholder paragraphs, ::space 4 leaves four lines of room. From ::name to ::end : ::note , ::tip , ::info , ::warning , ::danger , ::success and ::important are colored callout boxes ( ::note Your own title ). ::callout warning Title works too. ::columns 3 splits the text into columns; put on its own line to choose where each column starts. ::tabs with @tab Name lines, and ::accordion with @item Title lines, hide text until

Writeout and Bitbook have two ways to write a table. Pipe tables : one row per line, like Name Score , with a line of --- --- under the header row. Add a style after it, like --- --- {green} . The styles are blue (the default), green , purple , amber , plain and dark , plus four flat ones with no gradients or shadows: flat (gray, with a big rounded outline, thick lines between the cells, a darker header row and stripes) and its tinted cousins flatblue , flatgreen and flatpurple . Cell by cell : @@table [a1h:'Name',b1:'Score',a2:'Ann',b2:' O 9 '] names each cell like a spreadsheet (columns a to o, rows 1 and up) and gives its text in quotes. The text can use any Keydown, like chips and bold , and \' writes a quote. A style can follow the ] , like {green} . In a cell-by-cell table, an h after the cell name makes a header. A row is a header row when its first cell is a header ( a1h ), and then its whole row is headers. An h cell on any other row moves up to the nearest header row above it. Another header row further down starts a new part of the table: @@table [a1h:'Name',b1h:'Score',a2:'Ann',b2:' O 9 ',c3h:'Bonus',a4h:'Round 2',b4:'Score',a5:'Bob',b5:' 7 ']{green}

Open a fence with a language and a style in curly braces, and add a title after a bar! npm run build The styles are terminal, mac, dark, paper, blueprint, neon, ember, gel and diff. Add the word lines for line numbers, as in js{dark lines app.js}. The diff style tints lines that start with + or -! Inline code takes a style too, like ls -la {terminal}, Cmd {key} or x {neon}. The inline styles are terminal, dark, paper, blueprint, neon, ember, gel and key!

A line that is only ::pagebreak is a page break. In Writeout's Pages view the text after it starts on a fresh page, and printing starts a new page there too. Writeout's New Page button (or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter) puts one at the caret, and Backspace at the start of the next line takes it away.

::divider draws the aqua strip. Put a style in the braces for another look, like ::divider{wavy} , and add a title after a to run the line on both sides of it, like ::divider{poolside Lap two} . The styles are aqua, poolside, dual, notched, wavy, dotted, dashed, zigzag, glow, ruler, stitched, bubbles, scallop, neon, arrows, fade, swallow, triple, stepped, crest, ticket, gel, glass and rim. ::divider{aqua} the original aqua strip {aqua} ::divider{poolside} plain orange dashed lines, no special effects at all {poolside} ::divider{dual} a thick and a thin rail {dual} ::divider{notched} pointed ends and a V notch in the middle {notched} ::divider{wavy} a rolling wave {wavy} ::divider{dotted} a row of gel beads {dotted} ::divider{dashed} rounded dashes {dashed} ::divider{zigzag} a zigzag {zigzag} ::divider{glow} a neon line that fades out at both ends {glow} ::divider{ruler} ruler tick marks {ruler} ::divider{stitched} orange stitches {stitched} ::divider{bubbles} bubbles rising in the water {bubbles} ::divider{scallop} a row of little arcs ::divider{neon} a thin glowing tube of light {neon} ::divider{arrows} a row of little chevrons pointing right {arrows} ::divider{fade} a soft line that fades out at both ends {fade} ::divider{swallow} a two-tone ribbon with a V cut at each end, a cousin of Notched {swallow} ::divider{triple} three V notches in a candy-striped bar {triple} ::divid

Any named style can take one of 16 colors as a third part: ::divider{style Title color} . Leave the title empty to color a plain line, like ::divider{wavy red} . A color only works together with a style ( ::divider{red} is just the original aqua strip), and the title takes the color too. The colors are red , orange , gold , yellow , lime , green , turquoise , teal , cyan , blue , purple , pink , slate , white , fog , black . ::divider{wavy red} {wavy red} ::divider{poolside blue} {poolside blue} ::divider{dual green} {dual green} ::divider{glow pink} {glow pink} ::divider{dashed purple} {dashed purple} ::divider{scallop Title orange} {scallop Title orange} {scallop} ::divider{notched Chapter two} {notched Chapter two} ::console{warning: low battery} {warning: low battery} ::diff{+ added a new line - removed an old one} {+ added a new line - removed an old one} ::horizon (no text needed) ::waypoint{NAV: HOME // ALT: 0 FT} {NAV: HOME // ALT: 0 FT} ::entry{Today I learned about Keydown.} {Today I learned about Keydown.} ::draw (a drawing pad in Writeout)

::blank{style rows Label} leaves an empty box to write in, for textbooks and worksheets. The styles are box, dashed, lines, grid and dots. The rows are how tall it is (4 by default), and the label is optional. ::blank{6} is a six-row box. {box 3 Try it yourself} {lines 4 Write your answer} {grid 4} {dots 3} {dashed 3 Sketch it here}

[ 8] puts a blank to write in right inside a sentence, 8 characters wide. Leave the number out for a standard width. Add an answer after a bar, like [ 8 photosynthesis] , and it stays hidden until you click the blank (it never prints). Plants make food by [ 14 photosynthesis] using [ 6] and water. [ 6] is the same blank drawn as a small empty box instead of a line, and it takes an answer too, like [ 6 2024] . The war ended in [ 6 1945] and began in [ 6].

::pagenumbers{style start} is a small marker that changes how page numbers look from the page it sits on, until the next marker. The styles are none (front matter, no number), arabic , roman (i, ii, iii), upper-roman (I, II, III), alpha (a, b, c), upper-alpha , greek (α, β, γ) and upper-greek . The start number is optional and defaults to 1, so ::pagenumbers{roman 1} starts a Roman section and ::pagenumbers{arabic 1} starts the main text again at 1. Writeout and Bitbook show the numbers on their page sheets (turn on Page Numbers), and the marker itself never prints. In Writeout and Bitbook, use Layout Pages Page Number Format (or View in Bitbook) to place one at the caret!

Put these at the start of a line (both can go on the same line): {bar COLOR SHAPE LOOK SIDE WIDTH} a bar. Color: the 13 Annotate colors, black or a hex. Shape: solid (default), dashed , dotted , rounded , rounddash . Look: flat (default), gel (a glossy tube like the Gel Underline), aero (the notched divider's glass), neon , candy , double . Side: left (default) or right . Width: thin or thick . Example: {bar blue gel dashed thick} {mark SYMBOL COLOR LOOK SIDE SIZE POSITION label} a badge or label. Symbol: star bang ask check cross flag arrow heart idea note warn dot plus text ( text shows only the label). Look: flat , gel , aero , outline , plain . Size: small , large . Position: middle , bottom . Example: {mark flag purple gel large middle Review}

Templates are snippets of Keydown (the text Source shows). In Writeout, Insert, Templates opens a window with 13 pre-made ones (meeting notes, planners, a letter, a recipe...) and your own: save the selection (or the whole page) as a template, edit the text, and insert it. It goes in right at the caret: typed in at the cursor in Source mode; otherwise one line lands inside your words, and a longer template splits the line around it.

Three more gel marks, in all 13 Annotate colors, built like the Gel Underline (glossy tube, deeper edge, round ends): R words [ Gel Bracket: R words [ B words Gel Guillemets: B words PR words [[ Gel Double Brackets: PR words [[ By name they are R.bracket(words) , B.guillemets(words) and PR.dbracket(words) .

{tip red dashed Tooltip text}words{/tip} draws a colored underline and shows the note when someone points at the words (or tabs to them). The first word is the color (the 13 Annotate colors, black or a hex like ff8800), then one of straight , rounded , dashed , rounddash or dotted : {tip blue rounded A rounded blue underline!}point here{/tip}

Invent your own Keydown tag right inside a document! A line starting with @style defines it: @style ~~sale~~ { background: linear-gradient( ff8a00, e52e71); color: fff; border-radius: 999px; padding: 0 10px; } Then write ~~sale~~text~~sale~~ anywhere after it, and it draws with that CSS: ~~sale~~50% off~~sale~~! The opening and closing marks can differ, like @style <<star <<end { ... } , and &::before { ... } / &::after { ... } inside the braces add a little shine or icon. The definition travels with the document (it saves back to its own @style line), so a style you invent is yours to keep, share, or put in an OpenDB lite.

Write a little arithmetic right in the text, and it calculates: {{price 4.50}} sets a value and shows nothing at all (a line with only settings disappears). A value can be a number, a calculation, a percentage like {{down 3.01%}} or any words. {{price}} shows it as plain text, with no chip. {{price qty}} , {{money(price qty, "$")}} , {{round(x, 2)}} and more show a result. {{today}} , {{days until("2026-12-25")}} , {{year}} read the date. {{check paid}} , {{counter tickets 2}} and {{slider temp 27 from 20 to 34}} are things you can click, and the totals around them update right away. For example: {{price 4.50}}{{qty 3}}Tickets: {{qty}} × {{money(price, "$")}} {{money(price qty, "$")}} !

A line from ::name to ::end becomes something you can use, right in the text: ::chart bar line area pie donut Title then a table of numbers draws a chart. ::poll Question then option lines becomes something readers can vote on. ::quiz Question then option lines, with [x] option marking the right answer. ::scene holds a Zonerider scene (or a link to a .zr , .glb or .gltf file) and shows it in 3D. ::timer 5:00 Label and ::map 38.72, -9.14 13 Lisbon are one line each, no ::end needed. Seven more blocks: ::progress 70% Label or ::progress 3/5 Chapters is a progress bar (one line). ::countdown 2027-01-01 18:30 New year counts down live to a date, and an optional time (one line). ::rating 4/5 Great food shows stars, halves allowed (one line). ::steps Title then [x] done step and next step lines, then ::end , draws a numbered path with the next step lit up. ::stats Title then Label Value +change rows, then ::end , makes big number tiles. A change starting with + is green and one starting with - is red. ::fold Title then the hidden lines, then ::end , is a foldout you click open (write ::fold open Title to start open). ::timeline Title then 2019 - Started lines, then ::end , draws a vertical timeline. 70% Launch readiness 4/5 Great food

Underline, wavy underline and strikethrough each have their own marks, and each can have its own color! Put a color in square brackets right before the opening marks: a color code (R O GL Y L G TU T C B PR PK SL, the same ink colors as Annotate and Draw) or a hex : text underline ~ text ~ ~ wavy underline ~ (a fine wave, the same thickness as the straight underline) - text - - strikethrough - [R] text [R] red underline [ 2563eb]~ text ~ [ 2563eb]~ blue wavy underline ~ [G]- text - [G]- green strikethrough - In Writeout, the Font ribbon has an Underline, a Wavy Underline and a Strikethrough button, and each has an arrow with the Annotate and Draw ink colors (plus More Colors)! Write sp(text) to hide words behind a dark bar until someone clicks them, like sp(the butler did it)! Click again to hide them. Saved as text it stays sp(text) . The words cannot contain a ) .

Lines that follow each other with the same quote symbol are ONE quote with several lines: First line of the quote Second line of the quote A blank line (just the symbol) leaves a gap inside the quote Write it with at the start of every line (or ! , and the other looks: the symbol has to match). A line with only the symbol is a blank line inside the quote, a different symbol starts a new quote, and a line without a symbol ends it. In Visual mode Shift+Enter adds a line inside a quote, and Source writes each line with its symbol.

A line that starts with a symbol, and a space is a quote with a different look, like the plain quote but dressed up. They are all the same kind of quote, only the look changes. Type the line and press Enter (or use Re-format); saving as text gives the same line back. There are 14 looks: ! your text Orange: an orange tinted panel with an orange bar on the left, like the green and red looks. ! This is how a quote looks in the dashed frame look. ~ your text Whisper: small faded italic words behind a dotted bar. ~ This is how a quote looks in

Start a line with a mark and a space to make a bullet, and the mark picks the look. Lines with the same mark stay one list, and a new mark starts a new list! item is the round bullet - - item is a dash + + item is a green plus . . item is a ring ~ ~ item is an orange diamond item is a purple arrow

In Writeout (Insert Custom Emoji) and Bitbook (Skills Custom Emoji / Symbol) you can draw your own emoji or symbol on a square canvas with a pen, a gel pen, a marker, a neon tube or a dashed line, and it goes into your text like a picture the size of a letter. Double-click it later to keep drawing. Saved as text it is @@emoji "d 'g:ff7a1a:6:10,20;30,40',size 'md'" : each stroke is ink:color:width:x,y;x,y;... on a 100 by 100 square, strokes are joined with , and the size is sm , md or lg .
Saved files How Keydown is stored in .kd and .kn files, and the extra spellings that carry colors, fonts, sizes, alignment, pictures and tabs!

Writeout and Bitbook save their files (.kd and .kn) as Keydown text: a short header with the page size and other settings, then the document itself, readable in any text editor. When a file opens, the text turns back into formatting. A few extra spellings cover what the toolbar makes: Colors, fonts and sizes : [words]{color dc2626} colors the words, like [these words]{color dc2626}. bg gives a background, like [a marker]{bg fde047}, font "Georgia" picks a font, size 24px a size and weight 600 a weight. They can be combined: [big blue words]{color 2563eb size 20px weight 700} gives [big blue words]{color 2563eb size 20px weight 700}. Alignment : a line starting with {align center} is centered; right and justify work too. Pictures and files : a picture you inserted is saved right in the file as !name , with {width 240px} after it when you resized it. An attached file is report.pdf{file} . Tabs : each tab of a document starts with a line like ::tab{name "Ideas"} . Plain symbols : words that only look like Keydown keep their symbols as themselves, with a backslash, like \ R\ not a highlight\ \ .

h: Extras in Writeout, Bitbook and OpenDB
x: Math : $x^2$ writes math in a line, like $x^2 + y^2 r^2$, and $$ ... $$ gives a centered equation. An equation box with buttons helps you build it without knowing LaTeX. Double-click an equation anywhere (a Svelte component that only shows text, or a Plume piece too) and the same box opens to edit it; the new LaTeX is written back into the text it came from. Footnotes : [^1] adds a numbered note, and a line starting with [^1]: gives its text. Links : in OpenDB, [[entry-name]] links to another entry, and [[entry-name other words]] changes the words shown. Templates : in OpenDB, notices like {{stub}} and {{citation needed}} mark entries that need work. See the Templates page.

Keydown full reference This is the complete Keydown article from OpenDB, drawn here section by section with live examples. Pick a section below, or type in the filter to narrow the list. Every chip family, divider, quote look, text effect and block has its own section! Finding a style The Unique Styles and Style packs sections are huge, with thousands of designs. They are drawn only when you open them, so the page stays quick!

Keydown is the formatting language of [[radii-office Radii Office]]. Instead of clicking buttons, you type short tags around your text, and the text turns into formatting: G glossy chips , %B%gloss pills%, %O%gel flags%, @neontube-2@unique styles@, B gel orbs B , Y gel highlights , bold , headings, lists and dozens of interactive "applets". Many of its looks come from the [[frutiger-aero Frutiger Aero]] style. Every example below is drawn live, right on this page.

In Writeout and Bitbook, a tag turns into its formatting the moment you press Space after it, and pressing Enter at the end of a line formats every tag left on that line. In OpenDB, Phosphor and other apps, tags are drawn whenever the text is shown. Most tags wrap your text in an opening and a closing tag, such as R and . Typing \\ at the end of a formatted piece steps back out of it. Writeout and Bitbook can also Un-format a whole page, which turns all of its formatting back into tags so mistakes are easy to spot, and Re-format it, which formats everything again and underlines any tag that could not be formatted. Keydown text is saved in .kd files (Writeout documents and OpenDB entries) and .kn files (Bitbook notes), and those apps can open each other's files.

Start a line with one of these and a space: Heading makes a big heading, Heading a smaller one and Heading a third level. Heading , Heading and Heading make levels four, five and six. Heading makes the extra large mega header . item makes a bullet point, and text a quote. - text makes subtext : small, dim text for notes and fine print. - This is subtext, a bit smaller and softer than the text around it! Subtext can hold other Keydown, like bold and code . In Writeout and Bitbook, type - at the start of a line and press Enter, and pressing Enter at the end of a subtext line starts a normal line again!

bold gives bold , and italic gives italic . Backticks around a word show it in a code font. &&spark&& gives &&spark&&. &sparklet& gives &sparklet&, a lighter cousin of Spark Text with soft cyan words and a gentle glow. It needs a lone & hugging each side of the words, so things like AT&T and R&D stay as typed.

Underline, wavy underline and strikethrough each have their own marks, and each can have its own color! Put a color in square brackets right before the opening marks: a color code (R O GL Y L G TU T C B PR PK SL, the same ink colors as Annotate and Draw) or a hex : text underline ~ text ~ ~ wavy underline ~ (a fine wave, the same thickness as the straight underline) - text - - strikethrough - [R] text [R] red underline [ 2563eb]~ text ~ [ 2563eb]~ blue wavy underline ~ [G]- text - [G]- green strikethrough - In Writeout, the Font ribbon has an Underline, a Wavy Underline and a Strikethrough button, and each has an arrow with the Annotate and Draw ink colors (plus More Colors)! In Writeout (Insert Custom Emoji) and Bitbook (Skills Custom Emoji / Symbol) you can draw your own emoji or symbol on a square canvas with a pen, a gel pen, a marker, a neon tube or a dashed line, and it goes into your text like a picture the size of a letter. Double-click it later to keep drawing. h: Extras in Writeout, Bitbook and OpenDB
x: Math : $x^2$ writes math in a line, like $x^2 + y^2 r^2$, and $$ ... $$ gives a centered equation. An equation box with buttons helps you build it without knowing LaTeX. Double-click an equation anywhere (a Svelte component that only shows text, or a Plume piece too) and the same box opens to edit it; the new LaTeX is written back into the text it came from. Footnotes : [^1] adds a numbered note, and a line starting with [^1]: gives its text. Links : in OpenDB, [[entry-name]] links to another entry, and [[entry-name other words]] changes the words shown. Templates : in OpenDB, notices like {{stub}} and {{citation needed}} mark entries that need work. See the Templates page.
